sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File description and standard imports
sections.what: Describes what the tool does and gives example commands. Loads standard Python tools for arguments, files, text patterns, and time.
sections.why: Explains how to call the tool for anyone reading the file.

sections.name: load_env (part 1)
sections.title: Reading the API key from settings files
sections.what: Reads simple name and value lines from up to three possible settings files and adds any setting that is not already present in the environment.
sections.why: Keeps the API key out of the code and the command line.
sections.watch_out: A value already exported in the environment wins over the file, and an earlier file in the search order wins over a later one.

sections.name: load_env (part 2)
sections.title: Category list and model instructions
sections.what: Holds the list of icon categories and the two text templates that tell the model how to structure its reply.
sections.why: Keeps the instructions for the model in one place.
sections.watch_out: The templates ask for a specific code block format, so changing that format breaks code extraction.

sections.name: extract_svgs
sections.title: Pulling SVG code out of model replies
sections.what: Searches the model reply for SVG code, trying a marked svg block first, then an xml block, then bare svg tags. Keeps only results that look like SVG.
sections.why: Models wrap code in extra text, so this step finds the drawing inside the reply.
sections.watch_out: Matching is pattern based, so an unusual reply format can produce no icons at all.

sections.name: apply_color
sections.title: Applying the chosen color
sections.what: Swaps the placeholder color keyword in the drawing for the chosen hex color. If the color is still missing, it adds a color attribute to the root element.
sections.why: Lets the user choose a color after generation without asking the model again.
sections.watch_out: The change is a plain text swap, so drawings that do not use the placeholder keyword may not change color.

sections.name: apply_viewbox_size
sections.title: Setting the displayed size
sections.what: Changes the width and height attributes to the requested pixel size, and adds them if they are missing.
sections.why: Makes an icon display at a chosen size without changing its design.
sections.watch_out: The pattern changes every width and height attribute, including inside shapes, which can distort the drawing.

sections.name: generate_icon (part 1)
sections.title: Building the prompt and calling the model
sections.what: Checks for the API key, builds the full instruction text from the description, style, category, color, and size, prints progress, and sends the request.
sections.why: Gives the model the full context for one icon in a single request.
sections.watch_out: The token limit is fixed, so a complex icon can be cut off in the reply.

sections.name: generate_icon (part 2)
sections.title: Reading, adjusting, and saving one icon
sections.what: Reads the text of the reply, takes the first SVG found, applies color and size, and saves it to the chosen path or to a generated name with a timestamp. Returns the path or nothing.
sections.why: Turns the model reply into a usable icon file.
sections.watch_out: Only the first icon in the reply is saved, so extra variations are dropped silently.

sections.name: generate_batch (part 1)
sections.title: Requesting several icon variations
sections.what: Checks for the API key, creates the output folder, builds instructions asking for several variations, and sends one request. Extracts the icons from the reply, or prints the reply start if none are found.
sections.why: One request for several variants is more efficient than many separate calls.
sections.watch_out: The model may return fewer variations than asked for, and the request is made only once with no retry.

sections.name: generate_batch (part 2)
sections.title: Saving each batch variation
sections.what: Saves up to the requested number of icons as numbered files, applying the color to each, and reports how many were saved.
sections.why: Gives each variant its own clear file name.
sections.watch_out: The size setting is not applied in batch mode, so the viewBox only affects the wording of the prompt.

sections.name: generate_sizes
sections.title: Creating one icon at several pixel sizes
sections.what: Generates the same icon once for each requested size, saving a separate file per size and pausing one second between calls.
sections.why: Useful for producing matching sets for different screen sizes.
sections.watch_out: Each size is a separate model call, so the variants may not match each other closely.

sections.name: main (part 1)
sections.title: Command-line options and early exits
sections.what: Defines the command-line options for description, style, category, color, size, output, and batch. Handles the list options and stops if no description is given.
sections.why: Gives users a command-line interface with clear options.
sections.watch_out: The name option is used as the description when the prompt is empty, which can surprise users.

sections.name: main (part 2)
sections.title: Choosing single, batch, or sizes mode
sections.what: Checks the options in order: sizes first, then batch, otherwise one icon. Passes the options along to the chosen mode.
sections.why: One command handles all three ways of generating icons.
sections.watch_out: If both sizes and batch are given, sizes wins and batch is silently ignored.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Program start when run directly
sections.what: When this file is run as a program, it starts the main routine. When another file imports it, nothing starts.
sections.why: Standard Python pattern that lets other code reuse the functions here.

summary: Creates SVG icon files by asking Google's Gemini text model to write the SVG code, then saves the result to disk.
purpose: Produces vector icons for a product from a plain text description, either one icon, several variations, or the same icon at several pixel sizes.
why: Likely reason: SVG is plain text, so a text model can write it, and the files stay small and scale cleanly.
how: Loads the API key from settings files. Builds an instruction prompt from the description, style, category, color, and size. Sends it to the model. Extracts the SVG code from the reply. Applies the color and size. Saves one or more files, using a timestamp or a chosen name.
inputs: A prompt or name, optional style, category, color as a hex value, pixel size, viewBox size, output file or folder, batch count, and a list of sizes.
outputs: SVG files on disk and progress messages on screen. Functions return the saved path or paths, or nothing when a step fails.
risks: The prompt is sent to an outside Google service. The size step changes every width and height attribute in the drawing, including inside shapes, which can distort icons. Failures return nothing with no error exit code. The model may return text that is not valid SVG.
debug: Confirm GEMINI_API_KEY is set and the .env file sits where the loader expects it. Confirm the google-genai package is installed. If the message says no valid SVG was generated, read the printed reply. Open the saved file in a browser to check it. If sizes look wrong, check the width and height attributes.
